chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen who said: Amr ibn Shimr narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him), whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, would face toward the Qibla and then say:
'O Allah! Cause it to begin for us with security, faith, safety, Islam, and all-encompassing wellbeing.
O Allah! Grant us its fasting, its night prayers, and recitation of the Quran in it.
O Allah! Preserve it for us, and receive it back from us, and keep us safe throughout it.'

key_terms.الْعَافِيَة الْمُجَلِّلَة: All-encompassing wellbeing; sublime health that covers all dimensions
key_terms.تِلَاوَة: Recitation of the Quran; especially increased during Ramadan
key_terms.صِيَام: Fasting (sawm); the obligatory fast of Ramadan
key_terms.قِيَام: Night-standing prayer; refers to the voluntary Tarawih/night prayers of Ramadan
key_terms.هِلَال: Crescent moon; its sighting marks the beginning of the lunar month

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Ali recite when the crescent moon of Ramadan appeared?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam Ali (AS) — the Commander of the Faithful — had a regular practice of facing the Qibla upon sighting the crescent moon of Ramadan and reciting a supplication. This du'a asks God for the sacred month to begin with the blessings of security, faith, and wellbeing, and requests the ability to fulfill its three pillars: fasting, night prayers, and Quranic recitation. The triple structure of the closing petition — 'preserve it for us, receive it from us, keep us safe in it' — reflects the complete spiritual covenant of Ramadan: that it be given and returned in soundness.
